authority_order: explicit owner decisions in active product/design

baseline.current_corpus_relation: The 67-file current normative corpus is byte-identical to the passing subject.

global_definition_of_ready: Dependencies are merged on the selected baseline and exact evidence is current.
Governing paths and stable IDs are named; applicable DR ownership, constraints, evidence, and fallback are recorded.
Port, principal, authority, durable facts, failure paths, and conformance oracles are explicit.
No unapproved capability or partial provider path is reachable.
global_definition_of_done: Boundary values are immutable/versioned; external inputs validate and unknown values fail closed.
Transitions are explicit, failures are typed cataloged typed failure codes values, and uncertain effects reconcile or park rather than retry blindly.
Applicable timeout, retry, recovery, resume, preservation, and cleanup proof is recorded against the exact subject.
Applicable unit, contract, adversarial, replay, crash, provider, and E2E evidence is recorded; pnpm check, git diff --check, CI, and independent exact-candidate review pass.

universal_constraints.security: Least authority; credential names resolve only in memory; secrets never enter durable records, logs, evidence, or exports; hostile-input and redaction limits apply at every port; provider output never widens authority.
universal_constraints.retry_recovery: Only named cataloged bound classes controls apply. Retry a same-effect identity only after confirmed absence and recorded reauthorization; otherwise reconcile or park. Timers wake but durable facts decide.
universal_constraints.split_rule: Split contract/core from realization when external mechanism families, primary authority seams, independent provider qualification, or semantic acceptance oracles differ. The semantic half remains useful and green but unconfigurable until realization qualifies.

phases.name: substrate
phases.exit_gate: Hermetic graph and first deterministic replay evidence; no effect path.

phases.name: durable core
phases.exit_gate: Complete semantic ledger/registry/artifact contracts with scripted fault, recovery, and uncertainty evidence; selected file providers remain unreachable.

phases.name: envelope and intake
phases.exit_gate: Exact source contract/provider, preview and two approvals, qualified proof, and witnessed accepted/rejected acknowledgement; no Run on rejection.

phases.name: lifecycle and execution
phases.exit_gate: Scripted intake-to-candidate/rework/park/suspend path, qualified local workspace, bounds/capacity/obligation semantics; no acceptance or landing claim.

phases.name: acceptance and delivery
phases.exit_gate: Scripted E2E for Landed, Blocked, Rejected, and NotRun plus crash points; cleanup cannot alter outcome; Stopped closure remains phase 5.

phases.name: settlement and operator surfaces
phases.exit_gate: Stopped-from-every-position, reconstruction/export, and SDK/CLI/MCP parity evidence.

phases.name: real-provider closure
phases.exit_gate: Before the broader supported-profile claim: all supported-provider gates/profile evidence and GF-062's audit of all 56 imported dispositions; CF-GATE-PRODUCT itself is the pure conjunction of the 39 recorded suite results and every named element of the 44 settled product proof routes.

Local file ledger, registry, and witness storage remain unconfigurable until the exact CF-MECH-LEDGER result passes.
Local file artifact storage remains unconfigurable until the exact CF-MECH-ARTIFACT result passes.

Local command verifier remains unconfigurable until its exact CF-MECH-VERIFY result passes.

parallel_lanes: After GF-004, source-contract/composition and durable-core work may proceed independently.
After GF-010, controller/recovery, registry, and artifact lanes may proceed independently.
After GF-022 plus their respective complete prerequisites, GF-020 (GF-019), GF-025 (GF-010/GF-012), and GF-026 (GF-013) may qualify in parallel before converging at GF-023.
After GF-030 and GF-012, GF-031 may proceed; after GF-031 plus each lane's remaining prerequisites, GF-032 bounds, GF-033 workspace, and GF-034 session lanes may proceed in parallel.
GF-039 can qualify alongside candidate work after GF-033/GF-022.
After GF-040, review-publication and verify/finalizer lanes may proceed independently; GF-047 qualifies independently of final delivery.
After GF-054, CLI and private MCP lanes may proceed independently.
GF-060 and GF-061 qualify independently before GF-062.
gate_edges: No port traffic before DR-1 framing.
No implementation dispatch before GF-010, GF-011, and GF-015.
No provider reachability before GF-004, GF-022, and that provider's applicable exact mechanism conformance suite pass.
No Run before the witnessed GF-024 acknowledgement.
No acceptance before GF-040; no landing before GF-043 and GF-044; no cleanup before GF-046.

No product claim before GF-062's CF-GATE-PRODUCT pure conjunction of 39 recorded suite results and every named element of the 44 settled product proof routes; the broader supported-profile claim separately requires provider gates/profile evidence and the 56-import disposition audit.

DR-1.constraints: Strict versioned JSON, deterministic canonical bytes, runtime validation and golden vectors; reject encoding.
DR-1.alternatives: Other encodings only under an owner-approved later decision.

DR-2.constraints: Private pnpm packages follow dependency/runtime seams without moving authority.
DR-2.alternatives: Smaller private topology only if the same boundary proof holds.
DR-2.evidence: Graph/static boundary proof and independent-build fixture.

DR-3.constraints: Pure immutable reducer/selectors and explicit tables; unimplemented transition rejects.
DR-3.alternatives: Internal decomposition only below the fixed semantic kernel.

DR-4.constraints: In-process typed semantic ports; transport only at mechanism edge; unavailable provider cannot be reached.
DR-4.alternatives: Provider transport is delegated only after its port contract.
DR-4.evidence: Applicable exact mechanism conformance suite and authority tests.

DR-5.constraints: Initial providers are structured-file source, file stores, local Git workspace, local verifier, Codex sessions, GitHub delivery, and terminal/file notice.
DR-5.alternatives: Unsupported provider mode omitted, never waived or inferred.
DR-5.evidence: Exact real-provider mechanism conformance suite and provider gate.

DR-6.constraints: D11 file stores, separately trusted witness, protected/disposable separation, and FC-TRUST stop.
DR-6.alternatives: Physical representation only under the existing semantic contract.

DR-7.constraints: Private TypeScript SDK with thin CLI and stdio MCP parity; no direct internals/public stability promise.
DR-7.alternatives: No surface rather than a widened surface.

DR-8.constraints: Deterministic private testkit, adversarial/property/fault fixtures, and exact CER; absent proof cannot pass.
DR-8.alternatives: Harness internals may vary below recorded suite semantics.

DR-9.constraints: Approved defaults/ranges and immutable validated profile; out-of-range fails preflight.

DR-12.constraints: Work source and notice implementations use validated PORT-SOURCE exchange and fixed notice derivation.
DR-12.alternatives: Channel implementation may vary below the port contract.
DR-12.fallback: Reject source or retain undelivered notice.

closed.DR-10: Closed remediation constraint: provider real limits map into declared hard resource capacity; policy may only narrow; misdeclaration becomes bounded mechanism fault.
closed.DR-11: Closed remediation constraint: non-gating Operations are owner-frozen and fail closed by default; authority, acceptance, evidence, landing, and preservation paths are never non-gating.
